# Backlink Pilot v2.1 **[中文文档](README.zh.md)**

**One config, one command. Automated backlink submission for indie products.** > Built by an AI Agent ([OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)) during real-world link building — battle-tested on 30+ sites. **259 target sites** in [`targets.yaml`](targets.yaml) — 226 auto-submittable with bb-browser. --- ## Quickest Start — Claude Code (Recommended) > Have Claude Code? **You don't need to read any docs.** Three steps: ```bash git clone https://github.com/s87343472/backlink-pilot.git cd backlink-pilot && npm install claude # Open Claude Code, just say "submit my product to free directories" ``` Claude automatically reads `CLAUDE.md`, guides you through config, installs bb-browser, and starts submitting. Detailed tutorial: [docs/tutorial.md](docs/tutorial.md) | Full guide: [docs/guide.md](docs/guide.md) --- ## Manual Quick Start ```bash # 1. Clone & install git clone https://github.com/s87343472/backlink-pilot.git cd backlink-pilot && npm install # 2. Install bb-browser (recommended) npm install -g bb-browser # 3. Configure cp config.example.yaml config.yaml # Edit config.yaml with your product info # 4. Submit node src/cli.js submit futuretools --engine bb node src/cli.js submit https://any-site.com --engine bb ``` --- ## Engine Comparison | Engine | Setup | Pros | Cons | |--------|-------|------|------| | **bb-browser** (recommended) | `npm i -g bb-browser` | Real Chrome, invisible, OAuth works | Requires Chrome | | **playwright** (default) | `npm install` | No extra setup | Detected by anti-bot, blocked by Cloudflare | --- ## Commands ```bash node src/cli.js submit # Submit to directory node src/cli.js scout --deep # Discover form fields node src/cli.js awesome # Generate awesome-list Issue node src/cli.js indexnow # Ping search engines node src/cli.js status # Check submission history node src/cli.js bb-update # Update bb-browser adapters node src/batch-submit.js --limit N # Batch blog comments ``` --- ## Strategy **Why backlinks?** Google ranking = other sites linking to you = votes. More quality votes = higher ranking. ### Best channels by ROI 1. **GitHub awesome-lists** — highest ROI, permanent, $0, 5 min each 2. **Free directory sites** — 259 targets in `targets.yaml`, most auto-submittable 3. **Blog comments** — Website field backlinks, batch-automated ### Submission pace - 1-3 min between sites, 5-10 per day - **Never submit the same product to the same site twice** ### Sites to avoid | Site | Why | |------|-----| | IndieHub | Hidden $4.9 paywall | | OpenHunts | 51-week free queue | | toolify.ai | $99 | | Product Hunt | Anti-bot, manual only | --- ## Agent Integration ### Claude Code Clone the repo, run `claude`, and talk. `CLAUDE.md` is the instruction manual — Claude reads it automatically. ### OpenClaw ```bash ln -s ~/path/to/backlink-pilot ~/.openclaw/skills/backlink-pilot ``` Then just say: "Submit to free directories" --- ## Project Structure ``` backlink-pilot/ ├── README.md ← You are here ├── README.zh.md ← Chinese docs ├── CLAUDE.md ← Claude Code agent instructions ├── LICENSE ├── package.json ├── config.example.yaml ← Config template ├── targets.yaml ← 259 target sites │ ├── docs/ ← Documentation │ ├── index.md ← Docs home (VitePress) │ ├── guide.md ← Complete usage guide │ ├── tutorial.md ← Step-by-step tutorial │ ├── troubleshooting.md ← 20+ debugging notes │ ├── adapters.md ← Site adapters reference │ ├── contributing.md ← PR guidelines │ └── skill.md ← OpenClaw skill definition │ ├── src/ ← Source code │ ├── cli.js ← CLI entry point │ ├── submit.js ← Submission dispatcher │ ├── bb.js ← bb-browser wrapper │ ├── browser.js ← Dual-engine manager │ ├── config.js ← Config loader + UTM │ ├── tracker.js ← Submission tracking │ ├── captcha.js ← CAPTCHA solvers │ ├── indexnow.js ← Search engine ping │ ├── batch-submit.js ← Batch blog comments │ ├── bb-update.js ← bb-browser adapter updater │ ├── sites/ ← Site adapters │ │ ├── generic.js ← Universal adapter │ │ ├── saashub.js │ │ ├── uneed.js │ │ ├── baitools.js │ │ └── startup88.js │ ├── scout/discover.js ← Form field discovery │ └── awesome/templates.js ← Awesome-list Issue generator │ ├── tests/ ← Test suite └── bak/ ← Deprecated code (not tracked) ``` --- ## Developer ### Writing a new adapter ```bash # Option 1: Generic (no code needed) node src/cli.js submit https://new-site.com/submit --engine bb # Option 2: Custom adapter node src/cli.js scout https://new-site.com --deep # Then create src/sites/newsite.js — see docs/adapters.md ``` ### Running tests ```bash npm test ``` > Full debugging notes: [docs/troubleshooting.md](docs/troubleshooting.md) --- ## Contributing See [docs/contributing.md](docs/contributing.md). PRs welcome: new adapters, CAPTCHA improvements, bug fixes. ## License MIT ## Credits Built with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai). Browser automation by [bb-browser](https://github.com/niciral/bb-browser) and [rebrowser-playwright](https://github.com/nickthecoder/rebrowser-playwright).

Dandi API is a comprehensive boilerplate repository for building AI-powered micro SaaS applications. It provides a solid foundation with essential components and functionalities needed to run an end-to-end micro SaaS application.

The service itself offers powerful insights, summaries, and analytics for open source GitHub repositories.

**🌐 Live Application: [https://www.dandi.cloud/](https://www.dandi.cloud/)**

- **Rate Limiting**: Integrated rate limiting for API protection.
- **SSO Login**: Implemented Single Sign-On functionality.

title: samuel-howell/SIM
author: samuel-howell
body:
***S**imple **I**nventory **M**anagement and **P**roduct **L**ogistics* ![image](https://drive.google.com/uc?export=view&id=1WliiC62IAnbRIjaCLDmnzPm820IfNJJl) ## **Mockups**
## **Overall Summary**

SIMPL is a micro-SaaS application that is designed to improve the efficiency and maintainability of small and medium-sized businesses’ inventory and asset management capabilities. SIMPL does this by harnessing the power of Material UI, the Google Dart codebase, the Google Flutter framework, and the Google Firebase real-time database solution to provide a streamlined, simplistic, and elegant approach to inventory management and product logistics. Some primary use cases in which SIMPL excels is verifying and storing employee information, sharing databases between employees using invite-only security measures, generating QR codes for easy item tagging and tracking, scanning an item’s QR code to perform basic inventory tasks such as viewing item details, incrementing or decrementing item quantity, and building inventory reconciliation sheets. SIMPL also generates charts tracking item quantity over time, as well as store sales, so that users can make informed decisions about which products are high performers and which products simply cut into profit margins. Furthermore, SIMPL supports importing and exporting inventory data in CSV file format for further data manipulation in popular applications such as Microsoft Excel and Google Sheets.

## **What is the problem?**

In many small and medium-sized companies, inventory management is a burdensome and tedious task. Because of their size, many of these companies are unable to afford many of the more prominent inventory management applications, like Cin7 and Zoho. Furthermore, they have no need for many of the features that these applications provide, such as ecommerce integration, aftership tracking, serial number tracking, etc. These business owners simply need a way to keep track of what is in stock, what isn’t, and which items are providing the most profit. I saw this first-hand at the company I interned with in Summer 2021. Inventory reconciliation was being done by hand with paper every day. Employees would physically count the items on the shelves and mark the totals on paper to compare with what the online inventory was showing. When I asked the store supervisor about the reasoning behind hand-counting inventory, she said that she was unable to find a suitable software solution. As I began to research this issue further, trying to see if I could find a software alternative, I also started reading articles about how the outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic had many reconsidering their job prospects, and how this was spurring the Great Resignation, which has led to an outgrowth of entrepreneurship and the creation of many small businesses. According to the Census Bureau, more than 4.4 million new businesses were created in the U.S. during 2020 alone. Pulling inspiration from my conversation with my supervisor, and the research I had done around inventory management software solutions, I saw a niche market and the idea of SIMPL was born. This new market of fledgling business owners and entrepreneurs has untapped potential in the realm of inventory management software, and SIMPL aims to be the answer.

## **How does SIMPL solve it?**

SIMPL will provide a service that many small and medium-sized business owners will benefit greatly from, without having to rely on any outside partnerships or external relationships. Using QR code technology in conjunction with the SIMPL app on iPhones, Androids, or Web-based devices, businesses will be able to manage their inventory in a quick and cost-efficient manner. Because SIMPL is cross-platform, it will be able to quickly integrate into a company’s workflow regardless of whether they use Apple, Android, or the Web-based devices. Also, because of CSV export capabilities, inventory data obtained through SIMPL can be shared and further analyzed through other applications if the user chooses to do so. This makes SIMPL a great addon for businesses that already have some form of inventory management in place, while also providing a competitive alternative for those who are in the market for a completely new system. SIMPL was built predominantly for phones, because we wanted to provide a cost-efficient solution for companies that didn’t want to invest in barcode scanner hardware and software. Utilizing QR code technology, as opposed to conventional barcodes, information retention capacity is greatly increased, being that a QR code has up to up to a 30% error correction capability. This means that up to 30% of the QR code can be damaged, by fading, dirt, accidental marking, scuffs, etc. and SIMPL can still read the information stored in the code. As inventory is moved between locations and endures the wear and tear of retail, this will reduce the headache that comes with inventory becoming unscannable due to damage to the barcode. Additionally, due to the more compact form of QR codes, printing costs may be decreased by up to 25% in certain use cases. Concerning logistics, SIMPL is designed to simplify communication first and foremost. Users will be able to see who last interacted with any item currently in the database. They will also be able to quickly and easily share stores with other users. Along with customary item insertion and deletion, SIMPL is designed to store scan-in and scan-out data for each item, allowing the application to generate detailed graphs concerning item quantity over a period of hours, days, months, or a year. For each store, SIMPL will also highlight which items are low in stock and which items are most popular, which will aid the user in making informed decisions about what items to purchase in the future. SIMPL also features an inventory reconciliation scan option, which will allow the user to scan the product on the physical store shelves, export that data to a separate CSV, and then compare the Official Inventory CSV to the Inventory Reconciliation CSV in order to find discrepancies quickly.

## **Who is the Target Market?**

Right now, our target market includes small to medium-sized retail companies, employing anywhere from 1 employee to 1000 employees, that either do not have an inventory management system in place, or would like to integrate a lightweight, cost-efficient addition into their current inventory management processes. With smaller businesses especially, there is a need to keep costs low. In doing so, more money can be put back into the business in the form of inventory and advertising, allowing the business to expand its profit margin and market presence. SIMPL is a solution for businesses who need inventory management and product logistics on a budget. As businesses reach those higher profit margins and bigger customer bases, inventory management becomes increasingly more important. Built with this in mind, SIMPL helps businesses establish a baseline for good inventory management practices early on, without divesting key funding that should be going to promote the business’s overall growth. We think that this affordability factor will be the main draw for customers who want to purchase and use the SIMPL software. Also, because of SIMPL’s availability on the major technology platforms (Web, Android, and iOS) we aim to be compatible with most, if not all, of the devices currently in use in our target market. Beyond our primary customer segment in retail , we would eventually like to bring SIMPL to small manufacturing companies and build a material requirement planning feature into the app, but that will depend on future development.

## **What is SIMPL's competitive advantage?**

There are a few other inventory management apps currently in the market, but, to our knowledge, none provide cross-platform support, an updated UI built to Google Material UI standards, an inventory reconciliation feature, and other streamlined features built specific to small and medium-sized businesses at a competitive price point. Many full-fledged software solutions and competitors, like Cin7, Ordoro, and Webgility, suffer from feature bloat and contain many tools that starting entrepreneurs and business owners may not need. SIMPL challenges the assumption that all of these extra features are necessary for an efficient management solution. Our research showed that features that generated Bill of Materials, Manufacturing Orders, or Purchase Orders, or integrated Point of Sale systems, were often under-utilized by many smaller business customers. Many of these bigger software options also lacked mobile apps to serve in the place of scanning hardware. Concerning the lightweight app sphere, we found that current apps such as Sortly, TookStock, and Telesto were very uniform in function, and there was not much to differentiate between them. None of these apps allowed users to see change in quantity over time graphically. Sortly was the only application that allowed QR code scanning, while TookStock was the only app that offered a semblance of inventory reconciliation. SIMPL provides these niche features while also covering the standard basics of item cataloging, item insertion/deletion, store insertion/deletion, and store share features. There seems to be an assumption that these are the only features necessary for smaller business owners. However, the entrepreneurial spirit continues to expand as COVID-19 restrictions lift and people become increasingly more independent, and they are looking for smarter and better ways to work. These future innovators and business creators need a way to manage their inventory without getting bogged down in feature bloat while still being able to integrate newer inventory technologies like QR codes, and see data in a visual way with graphs and charts. Current options in the app market don’t provide all of these features in one package, and SIMPL can fill in that gap.

## **Competitive Advantage Charts** Web Software | Mobile Apps :-------------------------:|:-------------------------: ![image](https://drive.google.com/uc?export=view&id=1LUi98ABuqQvA7joXSc2Rl4ct4XVw2tVE) | ![image](https://drive.google.com/uc?export=view&id=1LXzn2vZXhxG3M5BA5eIoUyDP5Skcvt1y)

Strava-Tool ===========



> A personal side project with Strava API using Python. --- ### Motivation This project is my personal side project with Strava API. The goal of this project is to analyze my training data for better future performance, as well as to **hone my Data Analysis & Visualization skills**. The idea was originally coming from the fact that my increasing demands for uploading indoor cycling activity data to Strava, especially in the lockdown time of COVID-19. I usually did indoor training with Zwift during the weekdays and long weekend group ride on the weekend. When training indoors with Zwift, I used to also record my cycling workout with a bicycle computer, for more workout information like power zone, laps, time, etc. This means there will be two generated files pointing to the same activity in the end. If you have authorized Zwift to connect with Strava beforehand, each of your virtual ride data will be AUTOMATICALLY synchronized to Strava. That's really exciting and satisfying when you saw a Strava notification telling you that "Your activity is ready." after suffering on the saddle for hours. (You know that feeling.😉) However, as an engineering graduate student and bike🚴 enthusiast, I decided to to take more control over the whole interaction process with Strava, in order to know what's happening under the hood. Therefore, I disabled the connection between the two Apps, and started developing a toy StravaAutoUploader tool with Python as the starting point of this side project. Hopefully it could be someday extended to have some advanced features like Golden Cheetah, TrainingPeaks, for analyzing, tracking, and predicting my performance on the bike!

--- ### Features (__just name a few, not completed yet__) - Fixing and uploading workout (Ride, Virtual Ride, Run, Hike, etc.) activity files with the help of batch script automation using Task Scheduler (Windows) https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/43208378/126695209-51a2c492-9b8d-4668-808d-801e813fe502.mp4 https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/43208378/126695221-0dcaaa7f-4b31-4093-ad5f-548504a6f335.mp4 - Analyzing workout data using Pandas package e.g., - yearly summary (similar to [Strava Year in Sport Data Report](https://blog.strava.com/press/yis2020/)) - How many workout activities I did per month/week in a year? - How much time I spent on cycling activities per month/week in a year? - etc. - Visualizing workout data using Seaborn and Matplotlib libraries as well as Tableau software e.g., - heatmap - etc. --- ### How to use the code * [ ] Pipenv * [ ] https://selenium-python.readthedocs.io/installation.html#drivers * [ ] batch file * [ ] auth * [ ] config --- ### Good resources - Getting started with Strava API: - [Getting Started With The Strava API: A Tutorial](https://medium.com/@annthurium/getting-started-with-the-strava-api-a-tutorial-f3909496cd2d) - [YouTube Playlist "Strava API for Beginners", by Fran Polignano](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLO6KswO64zVvcRyk0G0MAzh5oKMLb6rTW) - Further development ideas: [Strava Labs](https://labs.strava.com/) - [Strava API Developer Forum](https://groups.google.com/g/strava-api) --- ### Support the project Whether you use this project, have learned something from it, or just like it, please consider supporting it by buying me a coffee or making one-time donations via PayPal, so I can dedicate more time on open-source projects like this. 💪🙃 Thanks!:heart: and Cheers!:beers: --- ### Contact If you have any question or suggestion, feel free to contact me at huaming.huang.tw@gmail.com. Contributions are also welcomed. Please open a [pull-request](https://github.com/huaminghuangtw/Strava-Tool/compare) or an [issue](https://github.com/huaminghuangtw/Strava-Tool/issues/new) in this repository. --- ### License This project is licensed under the terms of [![MIT](https://img.shields.io/github/license/huaminghuangtw/Strava-Tool.svg?style=flat-square&label=License&colorB=black)](./LICENSE).

**Samsung, LG, Roku or another non-Android TV?** CleanYourTV can't run there, but you can still turn off the tracking, step by step with your remote: [cleanyour.tv/not-android](https://cleanyour.tv/not-android) **The viral tweet:** [x.com/gathint/status/2111379569030939102](https://x.com/gathint/status/2111379569030939102) On 17 October 2026 I posted a before and after of my parents' TV, cleaned up by Claude Code over Wi-Fi. It reached 7.4M views, people started doing the same to their own TVs, and their replies turned into the lists here: 170+ TV models from 200+ contributors in four days. The repo was called tv-vibehack until the 19th; old links work. **Themes, switches and add-ons:** [cleanyour.tv/addons](https://cleanyour.tv/addons) **Official links:** the website is [cleanyour.tv](https://cleanyour.tv) and the code, launcher and tools live only in this repo. Other domains using the name, such as cleanyourtv.com, are not run by this project ([#1004](https://github.com/Gathin23/cleanyourtv/issues/1004)). ## How it works Android TVs have the same debug bridge as Android phones. Switch on USB debugging in the TV's developer options, allow your computer once, and the rest is standard Android tooling: | Step | What happens | |---|---| | **Back up** | The list of installed packages and settings. | | **Disable** | The manufacturer's telemetry, ad services, content rows and preloaded junk, with `pm disable-user`. Nothing is uninstalled, so a restore script can undo every step. | | **Install** | A small native launcher, made the default home screen. | **No root, no cable, nothing uninstalled, and a one-line restore if you change your mind.** The bloat differs by brand, so the prompt has your coding assistant discover it on your TV and ask before touching anything you might use. ## Quick start | You have | Do this | |---|---| | **A computer** | Use the prompt with a coding assistant: the three steps below. | | **A computer, no coding assistant** | Run the three steps yourself: the commands are in [Doing it by hand](#doing-it-by-hand). | | **Only an Android phone** | Use the community-built [Clean Your TV app](https://cleanyour.tv/app) by [@udhaykumarbala](https://github.com/udhaykumarbala): connect, analyse, clean, in about five minutes. No laptop, no coding agent. | The three steps below are written for a coding assistant: the computer needs to be on the same Wi-Fi as the TV, with a shell on it. Without an assistant, [Doing it by hand](#doing-it-by-hand) is the same job, run by you. Any of these work: Claude Code (on [0G Private Computer](https://pc.0g.ai/?utm_source=cleanyourtv&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=readme) or an [Anthropic plan](https://claude.com/pricing)), [Codex](https://github.com/openai/codex), [Gemini CLI](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli) or [Antigravity CLI](https://antigravity.google/product/antigravity-cli). | Where | What to do | |---|---| | **1. On the TV** | Settings → Device Preferences → About → press OK on **Build** seven times → back → Developer options → **USB debugging** on. If you see a Network or ADB debugging toggle, turn that on too. Keep the TV on. | | **2. On your computer** | Clone the repo and open that folder in your assistant (`git clone https://github.com/Gathin23/cleanyourtv`), then paste [`PROMPT.md`](PROMPT.md) and fill in your TV model. | | **3. The assistant backs up, debloats, builds and installs the launcher, and checks each step with screenshots pulled from the TV. With this repo as context it takes about fifteen minutes. ## What you get A home screen that looks like an Apple TV and gets out of the way: | Part | What it looks like | |---|---| | **A pitch-black home** | A dock of your four favourite apps in a rounded band, where Apple TV puts it. | | **A top shelf** | Names the focused app in large type, with an ambient glow in a colour taken from its artwork. | | **The rest of your apps in a grid** | Slides up when you press Down. | | **One floating glass highlight** | Springs from tile to tile. Set `show_stats` in config or a theme for one line under the clock: CPU, free memory and free storage. It stays off unless you turn it on, and it refreshes only while Home is on screen. | | **Themes and module cards** | Themes change colours, wallpaper, dock and columns without a rebuild, and module cards let other apps plug a tile in, only with your say-so. | And a TV that stops working against you: no sponsored rows, no "Discover" nags, no analytics phoning home, no apps you never asked for. | | | |---|---| | ![The top shelf names the focused app over an ambient glow in its colour](docs/focus-2-up-netflix.png) | ![The Inputs popup: HDMI ports with what is connected, AV and Live TV](docs/inputs-menu.jpg) | | *Top shelf and ambient glow* | *Inputs: HDMI with connection state, AV, Live TV* | | ![The grid with the glass highlight on a tile and its name beneath](docs/focus-1-fancode.png) | ![The Clock screensaver: a thin clock drifting over the glow](docs/clock-screensaver.png) | | *The grid, one glass highlight, the tile's name* | *Clock screensaver, drifts so nothing burns in* | | ![The aurora theme: a wallpaper and tinted pills, pushed without a rebuild](themes/aurora/screenshot.jpg) | ![Six columns and a six-app dock from a theme's config.json](themes/six-columns/screenshot.jpg) | | *Aurora theme, pushed with `tools/theme.sh`* | *Six columns and a six-app dock, same launcher* | | ![Moving a tile: held OK, chose Move, the tile is picked up and the others dim](docs/tile-move.jpg) | ![The App library: installed apps, one press adds an app back to Home](docs/app-library.jpg) | | *With `tile_menu`, hold OK on a tile, Move: arrows carry it, Back puts it down* | *App library: one press puts a removed app back on Home* | ## Supported TVs Anything running **Android TV** or **Google TV**. | Platform | What works | |---|---| | **Android TV, Google TV** | The debloat and the launcher. | | **Fire TV** | The debloat half only, since Fire OS will not hand Home to a third-party launcher. Add your list afterwards and the next person with your model skips that step: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Doing it by hand Everything the assistant does, you can run yourself. The tools need Python 3 and nothing else. `tools/tv.py` talks to network ADB on port 5555. If that port stays closed and the TV offers Wireless debugging with a pairing code (the Chromecast with Google TV and the Google TV Streamer do), pair it once with the stock `adb` and run `adb tcpip 5555` first, as [Troubleshooting](docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md#connecting) describes. ```bash python3 -m venv tools/venv && tools/venv/bin/pip install -r tools/requirements.txt export TV_HOST=192.168.1.50 # your TV's IP address tools/venv/bin/python -I tools/tv.py --probe # model, Android version, firmware tools/venv/bin/python -I tools/tv.py 'pm list packages' # one shell command on the TV tools/disable.sh examples/xiaomi-mi-tv-4a/debloat.txt # apply a debloat list tools/restore.sh examples/xiaomi-mi-tv-4a/debloat.txt # undo it, stock launcher back tools/venv/bin/python -I tools/check.py examples/xiaomi-mi-tv-4a/debloat.txt # what a firmware update undid TV_HOST=192.168.1.50 launcher/build-and-install.sh # build the launcher and make it Home tools/theme.sh themes/aurora # push a theme; --reset removes it ``` | Tool | What it does | |---|---| | [`tools/tv.py`](tools/tv.py) | Pure-Python ADB client: shell, batch, push, pull, reboot, and screenshots, optionally pressing remote keys first. Works where the stock `adb` binary is blocked. Optional [paired Google ADB backend](tools/native-adb.md) for encrypted Wireless debugging. | | [`tools/b64push.py`](tools/b64push.py) | Uploads large files such as APKs in base64 chunks and verifies the checksum. | | [`tools/relay.py`](tools/relay.py) | Forwards a local port to the TV's ADB port, for assistants whose sandbox can't reach your network. Listens on this computer only. [Guide](tools/relay.md). | | [`tools/disable.sh`](tools/disable.sh), [`restore.sh`](tools/restore.sh) | Apply or undo a debloat list, the undo from the state recorded before the change. | | [`tools/recovery.py`](tools/recovery.py) | Writes the record `disable.sh` needs to undo itself, and prints the restore batch. | | [`tools/check.py`](tools/check.py) | Compares the TV with the list that was applied, for what a firmware update undid; `--fix` puts it back. | | [`tools/adb-closed.py`](tools/adb-closed.py) | Checks that the TV's network ADB port is closed once debugging is off: exits 0 when the TV refuses the connection, 1 while it is still open, 2 when nothing answered or the check itself could not run. Details below.
Windows (PowerShell) Every script has a PowerShell twin next to it. On Windows with Android Studio installed nothing else is needed: ```powershell python -m venv tools\venv; tools\venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r tools\requirements.txt powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File launcher\build-and-install.ps1 -TvHost 192.168.1.50 powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\disable.ps1 -TvHost 192.168.1.50 examples\xiaomi-mi-tv-4a\debloat.txt ```
How the scripts protect Home The install scripts ask the TV which launcher owns Home and only disable one they recognise, the four in `KNOWN_STOCK_LAUNCHERS`: `com.google.android.tvlauncher`, `com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx`, `com.google.android.leanbacklauncher` and Xiaomi's `com.mitv.tvhome` (PatchWall). Pass `STOCK_LAUNCHER=` (`-StockLauncher`) to override, or `none` to leave it alone. `tools/disable.sh` (`disable.ps1`) applies the same rule before it disables anything: if the list contains the app that owns Home and no other app on the TV answers HOME, it skips that entry, says why, and disables the rest of the list. The setup wizard, the settings apps, a vendor `FallbackHome` and factory-test apps (Xiaomi's `com.duokan.factorytest`) answer HOME too and don't count. So a list applied before the launcher handover cannot leave the TV with nothing to start. On Google TV it also keeps the owner while setupwraith answers HOME and stays enabled (not listed, or kept for the Wi-Fi network): setupwraith answers ahead of an installed launcher that is not Home yet, so it would take Home. Run the same list again once `launcher/build-and-install.sh` has made the new launcher Home and the entry is applied; `FORCE_HOME=1` (`$env:FORCE_HOME`) disables it anyway.
Where your lists can live Debloat list paths passed to `disable.sh` and `restore.sh` are relative to the directory you run from, so your own lists can live outside the repository. Absolute paths also work.
## The microphone, and what can be said about it "Which of these packages is listening?" has no honest one-line answer, and a permission scan makes it worse: on many sets most packages run as `android.uid.system`, so fifty of them show `RECORD_AUDIO: granted=true` and none of them record anything. On others the microphone is in the remote, not the panel, and a package with no audio permission at all still sees everything on screen — ACR clients such as `tv.inscape.tvclient.inscapeacr` identify content from the picture and need only `INTERNET`. `tools/privacy.py` reports what the TV actually says instead of guessing: `TV_HOST=192.168.1.50 tools/venv/bin/python -I tools/privacy.py` prints voice, ACR and telemetry candidates in three groups, each with its evidence — named by the firmware's own `voice_interaction_service`, a known component from [`examples/`](examples/), or nothing but a matching name — plus whether the package declares `RECORD_AUDIO`, whether it shares the system UID, and whether the returned AppOps history contains microphone access. A configured mode or a rejected attempt alone is not evidence of access. `--write privacy.txt` turns the identified candidates into a normal debloat list, so applying it and undoing it are the commands you already use (`tools/disable.sh`, `tools/restore.sh`). Packages that only matched by name stay out unless you pass `--include-low`; they are the ones to check with `dumpsys package ` first. What the audit cannot do is prove intent. `appops` shows an op was touched, not what happened to the stream afterwards, and no scan of package names proves a TV is or is not recording. Disabling an assistant is a trade you make with a specific loss (the remote's mic button, voice search inside apps), which is why the report names that loss per package instead of calling it a win. ## The launcher A small native home screen for Android TV: **about 532 KB**, plain Java, built for TVs with 1 GB of RAM. No blur, no video, no network permission, no background services. The **TV** needs Android 8.0 (API 26) or newer: `minSdk` is a compile-time floor in [`launcher/app/build.gradle`](launcher/app/build.gradle), and the install script asks the TV for `ro.build.version.sdk` before it builds, so an older set is told both numbers instead of failing at `pm install` (see [Troubleshooting](docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md) for what is left on such a set). | What | How it works | |---|---| | **Configure** | Dock order, hidden apps, Live TV app, 4 to 7 tiles per row, reduced motion. All in [`config.xml`](launcher/app/src/main/res/values/config.xml) | | **Settings on the TV** | Hold OK on Settings for launcher settings. Optional `launcher_settings_button` makes a normal click open them directly; TV settings remain on the settings page and their app tile. | | **Themes** | Background, wallpaper and layout from a `config.json` pushed over Wi-Fi, no rebuild. ten ship in [`themes/`](themes/), the built-in `default/` included | | **29 languages** | Follows the TV's language, with a fully mirrored right-to-left layout for Hebrew | | **App library** | Optional: browse every installed app and add or remove Home shortcuts. See [the app library guide](docs/app-library.md) | | **Tile menu** | Optional (`tile_menu`): hold OK on a tile for Move, Remove from Home and App info. Off, holding OK opens App info | | **Module cards** | Any TV app can offer its own tile; you approve each one once. See [`docs/modules.md`](docs/modules.md) | | **Add-ons** | Optional apps that plug in as module cards, kept in [`addons/`](addons/) and never built into the launcher | | **Clock screensaver** | A drifting clock over the glow, so nothing burns in | | **Remote keys** | Keeps the Input, YouTube and gear buttons working after the stock launcher is gone |
Build it yourself It needs JDK 17 and Android SDK platform 34. On macOS: `brew install openjdk@17 android-commandlinetools` and `sdkmanager "platforms;android-34" "build-tools;34.0.0"`. On Linux the install script finds `~/Android/Sdk` and the `java` on your PATH.
Configure [`config.xml`](launcher/app/src/main/res/values/config.xml) sets the dock order, hidden apps, the Live TV package, columns (tiles shrink from 5 up), rows under the dock, an optional VPN app for the network pill, and `reduced_motion` for TVs whose GPU cannot keep up. Themes set the same keys plus a background colour and a wallpaper.
Launcher settings and the default home - Click **Settings** for the TV's own settings. Hold OK on it for its menu: **Launcher settings** (with `launcher_settings_button` a click opens those instead and the menu leaves the row out), **Native settings** where the TV ships a settings app of its own beside Android's - Xiaomi China, TCL/FFALCON and Fire OS are in `settings_fallback_components` - because that app holds pages Android's has no row for, such as Xiaomi's Account & Security with the ADB switch; **Module cards** with `module_cards`; **Edit dock** with `dock_row`; **Reorder apps**; and **Restart…** while `HomeKeyService` runs, which opens the system power menu (a launcher may not restart the TV itself). The launcher's own page has these rows, top to bottom: - **Reorder apps**, only with `launcher_settings_button`: OK picks an app up, the arrows move it, Back places it, and Back again finishes. - **Apps per row** 4, 5, 6 or 7; **Rows below dock** 0 to 3, how many rows of tiles stay visible under the dock band; **Dock band opacity** 100%, 70%, 50% or 30%. The last two only do anything while the dock is its own row (`dock_row`, on by default). - **Wallpaper**: one picture from the theme's collection (or its `wallpaper.jpg`), **None**, or **Theme default**. A pick holds that picture and stops the rotation until you choose Theme default, press Follow theme, or push the theme again. - **Animations** on or off, and **Advanced effects** (tile lift, icon zoom and smooth ambient-colour transitions; they may use more memory) once animations are on. - **Open on start**, only with `open_on_start_choice`: Off, or an app that opens instead of Home the first time Home comes up after the TV starts. Once per boot, so Home and Back still reach the launcher. - **Follow theme (reset on-TV choices)**, which clears every choice above. Pushing or resetting a theme clears them too. - **Choose default home** opens Android's home picker, and **TV system settings** the TV's own settings page. - **Change the default home:** Launcher settings and the optional Default-home tile (`show_home_settings_shortcut`) open Android's home picker. Choose the original launcher to stop using CleanYourTV as Home, or CleanYourTV to return. The original launcher must be enabled; if the install script disabled it, run the restore script below first. Some TVs provide no home picker.
Languages English, German, Danish, Spanish, Catalan, French, Russian, Serbian (Latin), Polish, Czech, Italian, Portuguese, Turkish, Arabic, Hebrew, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese (Taiwan), Thai, Finnish, Vietnamese, Bangla, Indonesian, Norwegian Bokmål, Swedish, Dutch, Uzbek (Latin), Ukrainian and Korean. The launcher follows the TV's language. Android 13+ can set it for the launcher alone: `tools/tv.py 'cmd locale set-app-locales com.gathin.tvhome --locales ca'`. Hebrew mirrors the layout: menu buttons on the left, date and clock on the right with the greeting above, dock and app rows starting on the right with matching remote navigation, the input selector's icons and labels on the right, and dates with the month prefix ב (for example, 19 באוקטובר). The Clock screensaver right-aligns its date and time. Russian covers every screen, including race weekends, festival greetings and the Shamsi date. Other languages keep their original layouts.
Module cards Any TV app can declare its own tile (label, caption, glow). The launcher asks you once per app, keeps it hidden by default, and remembers the answer for that app's signing key and card name. Hold OK on Settings and choose Module cards to change your mind. How to make one: [`docs/modules.md`](docs/modules.md); the contract: [`docs/specs/card.md`](docs/specs/card.md).
Clock screensaver Pick "Clock" in the TV's screensaver settings, or over ADB: ```bash tools/tv.py 'settings put secure screensaver_components com.gathin.tvhome/.ClockDream; settings put secure screensaver_enabled 1' ```
Remote keys - An optional accessibility service keeps the remote's **Input** button working on Google TV (`INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1` at install). - It can bring back other buttons only the stock launcher answered, such as the **YouTube** button (`app_keys` and `input_key_keycodes`, in config.xml or a theme; `HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1` reads `app_keys` too). - A `hold:` prefix on an `app_keys` entry gives that button a second app: a normal press opens the unprefixed app, holding for half a second opens the hold one (by keycode or `hold:scan:...`). An entry can name an activity (`package/.Activity`), such as an add-on's quick bar, instead of the app's launcher entry. - In place of an app, an `app_keys` entry can name an action: `back`, `home`, `recents`, `mute`, `sleep`, `screensaver`, `settings` or `wifi`, so a spare colour button can mute the TV or, held, put it in standby. - `HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1` also fixes sticks whose Home key sends ALL_APPS, and opens Settings from the remote's **gear** button, even one Android does not map (scancodes or keycodes in config.xml). - With `settings_key_panel` the gear opens a [small quick settings panel](docs/quick-settings-panel.jpg) over Home or any app: TV settings, Display, Network, Apps and Launcher settings.
Navigation and artwork Up and Down move one row. The top buttons never fall through to tiles, and Down from them returns to the dock tile you came from. The last focused app is remembered, and installing or removing an app refreshes the tiles while Home is open. App banners load at xhdpi or better, so low-density TV UIs do not downsample them before the focus zoom.

![gpu-unlock: full-speed tensor cores for GeForce RTX](assets/banner.svg)

### Your GeForce runs AI at half speed. This fixes it.

![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-2.0.0-76b900)![RTX 20 | 30 | 40](https://img.shields.io/badge/GeForce-RTX%2020%20%7C%2030%20%7C%2040-76b900?logo=nvidia&logoColor=white)![Linux](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Linux-informational?logo=linux&logoColor=white)![License GPL-2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-GPL--2.0-blue)![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/Zagitta/gpu-unlock?style=flat&color=yellow)

**Up to 2× FP16 / BF16 / TF32 tensor throughput** · **+25–55% LLM prefill** · **+25–50% fine-tuning** · **+30–55% image generation**

[Supported GPUs](#supported-gpus) · [Benchmarks](#what-you-get) · [Install](#how-to-install) · [FAQ](#faq) · [Support](#support-me)

---

NVIDIA ships GeForce cards with their tensor cores capped to **half speed** for
FP16, BF16 and TF32 math with FP32 accumulation, which is what nearly all AI
training and unquantized inference uses. The same silicon sold as an RTX A-series
or professional card runs at full rate. `gpu_unlock` removes that cap at boot,
before the stock NVIDIA driver loads. No patched driver, no VBIOS flash, nothing
to redo when NVIDIA releases a new driver.

---

## Supported GPUs

| Generation                | Cards                                                                                                                  | Status                    |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| **Ampere** (RTX 30)       | RTX 3050, 3060, 3060 Ti, 3070, 3070 Ti, 3080, 3080 Ti, 3090, 3090 Ti, plus RTX 3070/3080 Laptop GPUs                   | Stable, 100+ user reports |
| **Ada Lovelace** (RTX 40) | RTX 4060, 4060 Ti, 4070, 4070 SUPER, 4070 Ti, 4070 Ti SUPER, 4080, 4080 SUPER, 4090, 4090 D, RTX 4050/4060 Laptop GPUs | Experimental              |
| **Turing** (RTX 20)       | RTX 2060, 2060 SUPER, 2070, 2070 SUPER, 2080, 2080 SUPER, 2080 Ti, Titan RTX                                           | Experimental              |
| Blackwell (RTX 50)        |                                                                                                                        | Not supported             |

Laptops only stay unlocked if the dedicated GPU is never fully powered off.  
Many laptops power it down when idle, which silently resets the unlock. Turning  
off runtime power management with `options nvidia NVreg_DynamicPowerManagement=0x00`
in `/etc/modprobe.d/` helps on some models, but expect mixed results.

The exact PCI device IDs are in [`kernel/gpu_unlock/recipes.c`](kernel/gpu_unlock/recipes.c).
Linux only. For Windows see the [FAQ](#faq).

---

## What you get

The tensor core rate doubles. How much of that you see depends on how much of
your workload is FP16/BF16/TF32 matrix math, and on whether the card has the
power headroom to run it.

Dense matrix multiply (FP32 accumulation, stock power limits):

| Card | BF16 before | BF16 after | Gain |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RTX 3060 12 GB | 27 TFLOPS | 51 TFLOPS | +87% |
| RTX 3060 Ti | 37 TFLOPS | 68 TFLOPS | +82% |
| RTX 3070 | 40 TFLOPS | 72 TFLOPS | +81% |
| RTX 3080 10 GB | 65 TFLOPS | 113 TFLOPS | +73% |
| RTX 3090 | 75 TFLOPS | 125 TFLOPS | +65% |
| RTX 3090 Ti (450 W) | 88 TFLOPS | 157 TFLOPS | +80% |
| RTX 4070 Ti | 81 TFLOPS | 150 TFLOPS | +84% |
| RTX 4080 | 104 TFLOPS | 193 TFLOPS | +87% |
| RTX 4090 | 165 TFLOPS | 329 TFLOPS | +100% (peak MMA rate) |

The RTX 4090 runs out of power before it runs out of tensor cores, so large
GEMMs at stock power limits gain much less than the peak rate suggests.

Real workloads:

| Workload | Typical speedup |
| --- | --- |
| LLM prefill / prompt processing, FP16/BF16 or AWQ/GPTQ (vLLM, PyTorch, Transformers) | +25–55% |
| Time to first token | 25–30% lower |
| LoRA and full fine-tuning in BF16 | +25–50% |
| Image generation, FP16/BF16 (SDXL, SD 1.5, Krea, DiT models in ComfyUI) | +30–55% |
| Video generation, BF16 compute (Wan 2.2) | +15–20% |
| FlashAttention / SDPA kernels | +50–60% |
| llama.cpp / Ollama with quantized GGUF | 0–15%, mostly at long context |
| LLM decode / token generation (memory bound) | No change |
| INT8, FP8 and INT4 models | No change |
| Gaming and FP32 CUDA | No change |

Outputs are bit-identical before and after; only the speed changes. These
numbers come from the [compatibility reports](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues)
users have filed, where you can find full benchmark details and post your own.

---

## How to install

First run:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock
cd gpu-unlock
make install
```

Then append `gpu_unlock.targets=all` to your kernel command line, keeping
existing options:

- **GRUB (Debian/Ubuntu/Mint):** add it inside `GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT`
in `/etc/default/grub`, then run `sudo update-grub`.
- **GRUB (Arch/CachyOS):** same edit, then run
`sudo grub-mkconfig -o /boot/grub/grub.cfg`.
- **Fedora/RHEL:** run
`sudo grubby --update-kernel=ALL --args="gpu_unlock.targets=all"`.
- **systemd-boot:** append it to the `options` line in your boot entry
(`bootctl status` shows its location).
- **UKI / generated entries:** add it to `/etc/kernel/cmdline` and regenerate
your boot images/entries (e.g. `sudo mkinitcpio -P` for mkinitcpio UKIs).

# FAQ

- Q: Do you have a website/coin/installer?  
A: No this is the one and only OG source for gpu-unlock. Crypto, websites, installers and what else is not associated with this project or the developer in any way shape or form. 
- Q: Does this depend on a specific driver version? I see `610.43.03` is pinned.  
A: No the driver is only fetched to extract firmware this unlock depends on    
- Q: What about Windows?  
A: I don't run windows and don't plan to maintain it but [https://github.com/impacifist/Windows-GPU-UNLOCK](https://github.com/impacifist/Windows-GPU-UNLOCK) has built a port, YMMV.   
There are windows installer's floating around but I would recommend being ++**very**++ careful with those.
- Q: What about Blackwell (RTX 50)?  
A: Not supported and unlikely to happen.    
- Q: Why did Nvidia handicap my GPU?  
A: Market segmentation, they want businesses to purchase the professional cards without these limitations at significantly higher prices.
- Q: Does this hurt my GPU?  
A: It's very unlikely, this only unlocks a small handicap Nvidia has put in place to differentiate datacenter and professional cards from consumer versions. It may heat up your GPU slightly because it now does more compute but the standard throttling and power management remains completely intact and should downclock.    
- Q: How can I assist?  
A: Please consider [donating](#support-me) so I can purchase more GPUs <3

## Local build

Every build downloads the NVIDIA/CachyOS inputs over HTTPS and generates
firmware only in the build directory and the binary package. All three formats install through the same `make install-*`
targets. Packages are built from the working tree, uncommitted changes included.

Build, install build dependencies, and install the packages in one step
(asks for your sudo password):

```sh
make install        # detect the distribution and select an installer
make install-arch   # makepkg -sif
make install-deb    # apt-get build-dep, dpkg-buildpackage, apt-get install
make install-rpm    # dnf builddep, rpmbuild, dnf install
```

`make install` uses `/etc/os-release` (`ID`, then `ID_LIKE`) to detect Arch,
Debian/Ubuntu, or Fedora/RHEL/CentOS families. The RPM installer requires DNF.
For other distributions, select a compatible explicit target above.

`make arch`, `make deb` and `make rpm` only build. Debian and RPM packages go
to `build/deb` and `build/rpm`. The NVIDIA inputs are cached in
`~/.cache/gpu-unlock/inputs` (`make inputs`; override with `INPUTS=`).
`dpkg-buildpackage` itself never uses the network, so a clean-chroot build (sbuild or
pbuilder) needs `GPU_UNLOCK_INPUTS` pointing at that cache.
The `make dist` archive, the Debian source package and the `.nosrc.rpm`
contain no NVIDIA archives or generated firmware.

## How it works

This Linux kernel module combines the cmpunlocker's V67/PLM technique with the
pre-driver timing of the UEFI approach. At boot it runs the unlock, writes the
speed selectors (SS0 `0x88888888`, which selects the full BF16 rate, and the
4-bit SS1 `0x8` IMLA4) and performs an FLR before the unmodified NVIDIA driver
binds the card. It is neither a UEFI application nor a patched NVIDIA driver.

## Boot flow and opt-in

The packages put `gpu_unlock` and its firmware in the initramfs and load it
there, before `nvidia` can bind a card:

- **mkinitcpio:** `/etc/mkinitcpio.conf.d/zz-gpu-unlock.conf` inserts
`gpu_unlock` right before `nvidia` in `MODULES`, so a display card is blank
for as short a time as possible. Without `nvidia` in the image, it goes
last and still runs before an `nvidia` loaded from the root filesystem.
Images are rebuilt on install. mkinitcpio ignores drop-ins for an image
built with `-c <config>` or a preset `_config`; put `gpu_unlock` right
before `nvidia` in that config's `MODULES` yourself.
- **initramfs-tools:** `/usr/share/initramfs-tools/modules.d/gpu-unlock.conf`.
- **dracut:** `/usr/lib/dracut/dracut.conf.d/gpu-unlock.conf`.

With initramfs-tools and dracut, the module is built for every installed
kernel that has headers, and those kernels' images are rebuilt on install
and again on removal. Kernels installed later get the module and a new
image from the kernel's own install hooks.

There is no `softdep nvidia pre:` rule: kmod honours only the first
`softdep nvidia` line it reads, so other packages' rules (`nvidia-utils`,
`gddr6_hwmon`) would silently override it, or it would override theirs.

The module does nothing unless the kernel command line opts in:

```
gpu_unlock.targets=all                          # every supported unbound card
gpu_unlock.targets=0000:21:00.0                 # only these cards
gpu_unlock.targets=0000:21:00.0,0000:22:00.0    # comma-separated
```

Addresses are full PCI names as `lspci -D` prints them (hex digits in either
case), independent of GPU numbering and display role. An entry that is not
a supported card (see [Supported GPUs](#supported-gpus)), including `all` mixed with addresses, is logged and ignored.
The cards are unlocked concurrently, about a second in all however many
there are, and each on its own: a card that is already bound or powered
down is skipped. Bus mastering that the board firmware left on (Supermicro
X11 does this whatever its option ROM and bus master settings) is cleared
first; a card some driver already initialised is still refused. Then
`nvidia` loads and binds every card as usual.

The display card works too. Its firmware framebuffer (the boot console and
Plymouth) keeps running while the unlock's firmware steps run, and is
removed just before the card's reset, as `nvidia-drm` would do a moment
later anyway. Its screen is blank from that reset until `nvidia-drm` takes
over.

Loading the module by hand after boot does nothing to a card that `nvidia`
has bound.

Suspend to RAM powers the cards off, which resets the speed selectors. After
resume the module unlocks every card it unlocked at boot again, before
`nvidia` resumes it: its suspend notifier runs just ahead of the one `nvidia`
resumes its cards from (`NVreg_UseKernelSuspendNotifiers=1`, the default in
current drivers; `nvidia-resume.service` runs later still). This adds about a
second to resume. A card that kept power, as in suspend to idle, is still
unlocked and is only read. A card that `nvidia` has already resumed, or that is
bound to another driver, is left as it is, and the log says why. Add
`gpu_unlock.resume=0` to the kernel command line, or write `0` to
`/sys/module/gpu_unlock/parameters/resume`, to turn this off. Hibernation is
not covered.

Check the result with:

```sh
journalctl -k -b | grep gpu_unlock
lspci -nnk -s 0000:[ID]:00.0
```

To stop unlocking, remove `gpu_unlock.targets=` from the kernel command line;
for a one-off boot, delete it in the bootloader's edit screen. Removing the
packages also removes the module and the initramfs drop-ins.

If the firmware on a card never stops, the module logs it and keeps the DMA
buffers that firmware may still use until the next power off. Power off
before trying again.

The kernel module and local packaging are GPL-2.0-only. The generated buffer
derives from the pinned CMP reference; NVIDIA firmware remains under its own
terms. See `firmware/NOTICE.md` and `licenses/` for attribution and notices.
